liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mama Tried** (1 review): Weir's voice on Mama Tried is highlighted, followed by an Easy Wind jam [8]
- **Dancin' in the Streets** (1 review): Jerry's notes in Dancin' in the Streets resemble Dark Star from a 1967 Rio Nido show [11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Performance from China Cat Sunflower through Turn On Your Lovelight was described as pretty hot [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Cumberlnd Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [13]

## The recordings

- **gd69-12-07.sbd.owen.6958.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 105 min; rated 3.43/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is less hissy than older cassettes but remains too muddy for many listeners; Several spots of static are present in the Black Peter recording [1][3]
- **gd1969-12-07.141743.sbd.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: soundboard; 12 songs; 106 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Hiss is present at the start of the rare Black Peter opener [8]

## Around the show

- Show occurred the day after Altamont, with a sense of loss wrapped around every note [5]
- Pigpen ends the show with a twenty-eight minute segment [6]
- Doubt exists about whether Black Peter truly opened the show, possibly due to missing earlier songs [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-12-07.sbd.owen.6958.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by The Wizard; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Source was a degraded SBD tape with almost no high end and several flaws [1]
- **gd1969-12-07.141743.sbd.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > Bear's cassette master (probably) > dat (Rob Eaton) > dat (44k) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav… [2]
